newsitem.title: JORDAN: Family of alleged NY bomb plotter say he innocent.
newsitem.headline: Family of alleged NY bomb plotter say he innocent.

text.p: The family of a Palestinian arrested in an alleged suicide bomb plot in New York said on Friday he grew up avoiding trouble and earned the trust of Jewish employers in Israel before heading to the United States.
Lafi Khalil, 22, was one of three Middle Eastern men arrested on Thursday over an alleged plot to attack New York City's subway system with a suicide bomb.
But his family in Jordan said he steered away from problems while growing up in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, where he witnessed clashes by Israeli soldiers in his home village Ajul.
"I never saw in his hand a weapon or saw a Palestinian flag or saw in his hands anything, he was always staying at home," his mother said, recalling the days before she and her family came to Jordan.
The family of Khalil lives in a modest dwelling in the town of Queira nearly 300 km (188 miles) south of Amman on the main highway to the Red sea port city of Aqaba.
They said Khalil even won the trust of his Jewish employers during the four years he spent making a living as labourer.

A Jewish restaurateur for whom Khalil worked in Tel Aviv even gave him lodgings at the premises where he helped foil an armed robbery by alerting the police at risk to his own life, his mother said, recalling her son telling her the story.

"If my son had wanted to attack Jews he was working with..., if my son wanted to do this thing in Tel Aviv, in Jerusalem he would have done it a long time ago," she protested, adding that Khalil never got into trouble or was arrested during those years.
Khalil went to the United States only last December to seek a better future after more than four years of irregular manual work in Israel, she said.

Both Khalil and a man charged with him, Gazi Ibrahim Abu Mezer, 23, were shot and wounded by police when agents raided a ramshackle Brooklyn apartment where, according to investigators, they discovered five pipe bombs.
Both men were in hospital on Friday recovering from surgery for multiple bullet wounds.
A third man was being questioned by agents from the Joint Terrorist Task Force of local, state and federal agencies, officials said in New York.

U.S. law-enforcement authorities said there appeared to be no evidence directly linking the arrested men with Wednesday's double suicide bombing of a Jerusalem market which killed 15 people, including the attackers, and wounded 170.
But U.S. investigators said the suspects intended to target Americans and Jews.
Khalil's sister, Lamis, a university student, said she had spoken to her brother only last Tuesday when he told her he was doing fine working in a supermarket in New York.
"He said that life was expensive in New York and that he was living with nice Arab boys and had also gotten to know an American girl," Lamis said.
"He was living in Israel for over four years and was living on his own and no one was complaining about him nor did he complain about anyone," she said.

"This thing he has been accused of I cannot believe, he never thought of anything like this, and to participate in such a thing, it's just impossible...I still cannot believe this and I hope he will be freed and it's just a suspicion."
The charges against Abu Mezer and Khalil include conspiracy to damage and destroy buildings and vehicles with explosives.
